title: libyas noc reports drone attack attempt fuel depot 2026 09 03
text:
TRIPOLI, Sept 3 (Reuters) - A remote-controlled drone attack targeted a fuel depot in Libya's capital ​Tripoli on Thursday, causing minor damage, the ‌state-owned National Oil Corporation (NOC) said in a statement.
The NOC said that technical teams had begun drawing fuel from ​the tanks to reduce the fuel level ​as a precaution. There was no immediate claim ⁠of responsibility and authorities did not say ​who they believed was behind the attack.
The attack caused ​minor damage to some pipelines and tanks no. 213 and 220 due to falling shrapnel, said Ahmed Al-Masallati, spokesperson ​for Brega Petroleum Marketing, which is in charge ​of Libya's fuel supplies.
No casualties were reported and the incident ‌did ⁠not impact supply operations.
Libyan oil facilities have been subject to repeated attacks and closures for various political and technical reasons since the 2011 uprising ​that toppled Muammar ​Gaddafi and ⁠set off a prolonged period of chaos.
In August, fuel storage tanks at ​the nearby Zawiya oil complex, in western ​Tripoli, were ⁠targeted by several explosive-laden drone strikes that hit one of the tanks and completely burned it.
Attempts ⁠to target ​oil facilities represent "a direct threat ​to the supply system," the NOC said in the statement.
